subject.title: chore(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Do the security and workflow owners approve landing these 14 grouped action upgrades across the secret-bearing CodeQL, token, Docker publishing, and Codex agent workflows?
rationale: The diff is mechanically clean and SHA-pinned, but CI cannot fully settle the supply-chain and privileged-runtime implications of replacing executable action code across several owner boundaries.

options.title: Approve after refreshed proof
options.body: Rebase or regenerate the branch, require exact-head green checks and secops/workflow-owner review, then land the grouped update.

options.title: Split privileged updates
options.body: Separate Codex, token, CodeQL, and Docker publishing actions from routine toolchain and housekeeping upgrades for narrower review and rollback.

options.title: Hold the group
options.body: Leave the current pins in place and wait for a later regenerated dependency update if owners do not accept the combined risk.

recommendation.title: Approve after refreshed proof
recommendation.body: Rebase or regenerate the branch, require exact-head green checks and secops/workflow-owner review, then land the grouped update.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS explicitly assigns several security-sensitive workflows in this grouped update to that team. ([github.com](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS))
